items.found: The main menu is organized around a new family's questions: About, Academics (Preschool, Elementary, Junior/Senior High), Admissions, and Student Life come first. Current-family items like the Lunch Menu, calendars, and FACTS Login are tucked under Eagle Essentials, which keeps them out of a prospective parent's way.

Pages are broken into short, easy-to-scan sections. Each homepage block has a heading, two or three sentences, and a Learn More button, and the Admissions page lays out its process under clear step headings.

The hero headline, "Uniting a Passion for Christ with Excellence in Academics!", tells a parent this is a Christ-centered, academically serious school. The Visit Us button in the header and the quick links just below the hero (Application Process, Schedule a Tour) give a clear next step. What the hero doesn't say is where the school is or which grades it serves.
items.rec: Add a short supporting line under the headline, such as "Preschool through 12th grade in Chickamauga, Georgia."
evidence: Uniting a Passion for Christ with Excellence in Academics

items.found: The homepage walks a new family through the school in a sensible order: beliefs, academics by grade band, admissions, athletics, fine arts, and the church partnership, ending with an invitation to a personal tour. Current-family content is kept to a single quick link.
evidence: Experience what God is doing at OCA through a personal tour

items.found: Oakwood is clearly Christ-centered. The homepage leads with a Statement of Beliefs and the partnership with Oakwood Baptist Church, and the Admissions page describes "Kingdom Education." But there is no page dedicated to spiritual life, so a parent can't see what discipleship looks like day to day: chapel, Bible class, prayer, or service.
items.rec: Add a Spiritual Life page that shows discipleship in practice, with photos, a short description of chapel and Bible curriculum, and a quote from a teacher or parent.

items.found: The Admissions page lays out a clear, numbered process in plain text: a private tour, the application, an admissions assessment, and notification. Each step says what happens and what comes next.

The header has the right action: Visit Us, which opens online tour booking. Beside it, Support Us is a dark navy button that draws the eye before the gold Visit Us button does. Further down, the Inquire Today button goes to the Admissions page rather than an inquiry form.
items.rec: Make Visit Us the most prominent button in the header and give Support Us a quieter style. Point Inquire Today straight to the tour booking.

items.found: Every path a family can take is short. The contact form asks for a name, email, and message, and tours are booked online in a few clicks by grade group (Preschool, Lower School, Grade School, Upper School). The longer application comes after the tour, which is the right order.
evidence: Online self-booking, 30-minute tours by grade group
Following your campus tour, you'll receive an email with a link to complete the Admissions Application

items.found: The About page lists four accreditations (NACSAA, NCPSA, AACS, and GAPSAC) and shows their logos. We didn't find news or media coverage anywhere on the site.
items.rec: Put the accreditation logos in the footer of every page, and add a short news or "In the community" section to the homepage.
evidence: North American Christian School Accrediting Agency
National Council of Private School Accreditation

items.found: There is no email opt-in or downloadable guide anywhere on the site.
items.rec: Offer a simple guide parents want, such as "How to Pay for Christian School in North Georgia: Tuition, GOAL Scholarships and Payment Plans." Oakwood already has the content on its Financial Information page.
evidence: Tuition and Fee Structure 2026-2027 School Year

items.found: Families who aren't ready to visit have several next steps: Learn More buttons for each program, the Application Process and Calendar quick links, Contact Us, and the church's website. There's no open house invitation or newsletter signup.
We didn't find any parent or student testimonials on the pages we reviewed. The quotations on the site are Scripture and the mission statement.
items.rec: Add 3 or 4 short parent quotes to the homepage and Admissions page. Facebook recommendations from current families are a good place to start.
